title: When Predicted Grades Don't Match Your Target
summary: Learn what happens when IB predicted grades miss university targets, how to adjust your list, request a review, and act before deadlines.
body_markdown:
If your IB predicted grades do not match your target university's requirements, you are not automatically barred from applying. However, your chance of receiving an offer may fall, especially when the course treats its published grades as a firm academic threshold. Identify the exact gap, ask whether your school can review the prediction before submission, and build a balanced university list.


The consequences also depend on the admissions system. UK universities commonly use predictions when deciding whether to make conditional offers, while universities in the US and Canada may consider them alongside transcripts, essays, recommendations, activities, interim results, and school context.


### What universities may do when predictions are too low


A university may:


- **Reject the application** , particularly if you miss a firm minimum or required Higher Level grade.
- **Continue assessing it holistically** because grades are only one part of selection.
- **Make a conditional offer at the standard requirement** , despite a small predicted shortfall.
- **Consider contextual information** if you qualify under its policy.
- **Request interim grades** or offer an alternative course or foundation route.


Published entry requirements describe the academic profile a university normally expects, but their meaning varies by institution and course. Highly selective courses may have many applicants who already exceed the stated level, so even a one-point gap can matter. Conversely, meeting the published grades never guarantees admission when tests, interviews, written work, references, portfolios, or contextual factors also influence selection.


### Identify the type of mismatch


Do not consider only your total out of 45. Universities often specify both an overall Diploma score and particular HL or subject grades.


Type of gap Example Likely significance


Overall total Predicted 36, requirement 38 Potentially serious, depending on course policy


HL profile Predicted 6,6,5, requirement 6,6,6 Important because the offer may require that exact pattern


Required subject Predicted 5 in HL Mathematics, requirement 6 Often more serious than a gap in an unrelated subject


Subject eligibility Wrong Mathematics course or level May make you ineligible regardless of total points


Read the current course page rather than relying on rankings, old prospectuses, or forums. Oxford, for example, publishes course-specific IB requirements that commonly include totals of 38-40 with specified HL grades.[UCAS entry requirements guidance](https://www.ucas.com/applying/you-apply/what-and-where-study/entry-requirements) also distinguishes standard requirements from contextual admissions, while warning that historical outcomes cannot predict an individual decision.


### What to do before applications are submitted


Your school's internal prediction deadline may be earlier than the public university deadline. Treat that internal date as the deadline for resolving questions or requesting a review.


### Confirm what will be submitted


Ask your counsellor or IB coordinator for your predicted total, six subject predictions, estimated TOK and Extended Essay points, the evidence used, the school's review policy, and the final submission date. The[RevisionDojo guide to when IB predictions are set](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/when-and-how-are-predicted-grades-predicted-in-ib-a-clear-guide-for-students-and-parents) explains common approaches, but your school's policy controls its process.


### Request a review based on evidence


Do not ask for a higher prediction only because a university requires it. Ask what evidence would justify reconsideration, such as a recent timed assessment, sustained improvement, stronger rubric-level coursework, or correction of a recording error.


A useful question is: "My current prediction is a 5, and the course requires a 6. Which evidence separates my work from a 6, and is there another assessment before predictions are finalised?" This requests academic clarification rather than special treatment.


### Measure the gap honestly


Compare your official prediction, recent timed performance, and the course's current overall and subject requirements. The[IB Grade Calculator](https://www.revisiondojo.com/grade-calculator) can provide an indicative profile from practice marks, but it cannot replace the prediction submitted by your school.


If all three measures are close, an ambitious application may be defensible. If your independent evidence also remains substantially below the target, revising the university list is safer than assuming your prediction will increase.


### Rebalance your choices


A balanced list includes ambitious choices where you are near the expected profile, realistic choices where you match it, and safer choices where you exceed it. There is no universal allocation because competitiveness, contextual eligibility, admissions tests, costs, and location all matter. A university is not a genuine safer choice if you would refuse to attend it.


Current position Sensible response


One point below overall, with required HL grades met Check the policy, consider applying, and balance other choices


One grade below in a required HL subject Ask admissions for clarification and include suitable alternatives


Several points below the requirement Treat the course as highly ambitious


Prediction may change before submission Gather evidence and use the school's review process promptly


Predictions already submitted Ask about permitted updates, but do not assume reconsideration


Improvement is likely only in final exams Consider applying later with achieved results


Foundation years and related courses may provide other routes, but they have separate academic and financial implications. Never assume that transferring into the original course will be straightforward.


### How the application system affects the answer


### UK applications through UCAS


UCAS describes a predicted grade as the grade a school or college believes an applicant is likely to achieve in positive circumstances. Universities decide how to use predictions alongside the rest of the application.


For **2027 entry** , the deadline is **15 October 2026 at 18:00 UK time** for Oxford, Cambridge, and most medicine, dentistry, and veterinary medicine or science courses. The equal consideration deadline for most other undergraduate courses is **13 January 2027 at 18:00 UK time** . Schools may set much earlier deadlines.


Predicted grades cannot normally be changed after a UCAS application is sent. Genuine data-entry errors may sometimes be reported, but correction does not guarantee reconsideration. Verify the current[UCAS application dates](https://www.ucas.com/applying/applying-to-university/dates-and-deadlines-for-uni-applications) before submitting.


### US, Canadian, and other applications


US universities set their own document requirements. A college may consider predictions alongside the transcript, school report, recommendation, midyear report, and final report, so there is no universal predicted IB cutoff.


Canadian procedures also vary. UBC states that initial IB decisions use interim grades and final IB results confirm admission. For any international application, verify who submits predictions, whether later grades are considered, and which final results are required to retain an offer.


### Improve your evidence strategically


Prioritise subjects where one grade increase would materially affect eligibility, especially required HL subjects. Each week, identify one recurring weakness, review it, complete targeted questions under controlled conditions, classify lost marks, correct the problem, and finish with a longer timed section.


The[Questionbank practice guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-question-bank-or-how-to-use-it-effectively) explains how to structure targeted work, while[Mock Exams and Exam Mode](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-mock-exams) test whether improvement survives time pressure. Jojo AI can clarify errors and command terms, but the strongest evidence for a school review remains your own assessed performance.


### Common mistakes


- Applying only to courses above your predicted profile.
- Comparing total points while ignoring required HL grades.
- Pressuring teachers without assessment evidence.
- Assuming a strong essay overrides an academic minimum.
- Submitting before resolving prediction questions.
- Neglecting final-exam preparation after receiving an offer.


### Conclusion


Predicted grades below your target do not always end an application, but they should change your planning. Identify whether the gap concerns the total, HL profile, or required subject; request any evidence-based review before submission; and retain realistic choices.


RevisionDojo's Grade Calculator, Questionbank, Study Notes, Jojo AI, and Mock Exams can help you build stronger, repeatable academic evidence while your counsellor helps you create a realistic university list.
